summary: Reserved pool warmup causing transient p95/p99 latency spikes and priority inversion with on-demand tenants
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightDocs is observing intermittent p95/p99 latency spikes and token throttling across their dedicated reserved pool. Spikes occur during short bursts (1–5 minutes) after a period of low activity and correlate with a high rate of prefetch/eviction churn on the GPU nodes. Symptoms point to priority inversion where on-demand/burst allocations trigger kernel preemptions and eviction storms that delay warmup of pinned reserved workers, causing downstream queueing and token-level throttling at the API layer.

Impact:
- BrightDocs reports elevated p95/p99 for generate and streaming requests; customer-facing features degrade for end users.
- Observed increased 429s/timeouts for some high-concurrency routes routed to the dedicated pool.
- Customer is on a committed reserved pool; they expect predictable latency.

Environment:
- Dedicated reserved pool in us-east, mixed GPU types (A10g + A100 lite).
- Autoscaler: predictive+threshold policy; burst capacity enabled.
- Workload mix: short chat-style requests (seq len < 512) and occasional long-context tests.

Why unique/important:
This is not a simple capacity shortage: nodes have spare GPU memory and utilization looks moderate, but eviction/reload churn at the driver/kernel level is causing transient throughput regression. The packet of behavior suggests scheduling/kernel preemption interactions with our eviction prefetch logic and the autoscaler's burst routing rules.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Simulate low baseline load on reserved pool for 10+ minutes (idle warm cache).
2) Fire a sustained burst of short concurrent requests (50–200 RPS) with mixed routes pinned to reserved pool; include on-demand burst traffic aimed at same region.
3) Observe p95/p99 latency spikes within 30–90s of burst start and increased eviction/prefetch log lines on affected nodes.
4) Reduce burst; note that latencies take ~2–6 minutes to return to baseline depending on kernel cache warmup and batching behaviour.

investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: autoscaler burst routing will place on-demand bursts onto shared nodes and occasionally trigger kernel-level preemption of reserved workers. When reserved workers are preempted, their KV caches + eager-prefetch window are invalidated leading to a rebuild cost that inflates tail latencies. Observed correlation between preempt events and first request latency for the next 50–200 requests.

What we checked:
- Node-level GPU memory usage and process lists: no out-of-memory; memory free but frequent allocation/free patterns seen.
- Kernel driver logs: repeated page migration/eviction entries matching timestamps of spikes.
- Routing decisions: short window where policy allowed placement of on-demand tasks on same node due to aggressive burst allowance.
- Autoscaler logs: predictive policy mis-specified affinity thresholds caused burst placements to favor shared nodes rather than cold-start new reserved nodes.

Hypotheses to validate:
- Lowering on-node preemption frequency (stronger isolation) will reduce p99.
- Tuning prefetch eviction policy to be more conservative on reserved pool will reduce rebuild cost.
- Autoscaler policy change: prefer new node allocation for burst if reserved-workers would be preempted.

Temporary mitigations tried:
- Disabled burst-placement-to-shared for BrightDocs (immediate reduction in p99 within 3 minutes).
- Applied a conservative eviction window (increasing retention) for reserved pool; observed reduced KV reload counts.

Remaining unknowns:
- Exact kernel-level threshold where eviction cost dominates vs. capacity tradeoffs for cold-start vs. preemption.
- Potential impact on overall cluster utilization if we restrict burst placements.

resolution:
Workaround implemented: disabled burst placement to shared nodes for BrightDocs' reserved pool and applied a conservative eviction window for reserved workers. Short-term results: p95 reduced by ~38% and p99 by ~54% for observed bursts.

Planned permanent actions:
- Implement autoscaler rule change to prefer new node allocation over preempting reserved workers when predicted burst would cause >20% eviction churn. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1423)
- Add telemetry to detect preemption-induced eviction storms and auto-disable burst placement for affected pools until warmup completes.
- Follow-up runbook and SLO communication to customer, including expected recovery times and operational tradeoffs.
